To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people can improve the realism of confidence judgments, and that they can do so by deselecting the judgments with the least realistic values.

people can increase the realism in their meta-metacognition judgments by excluding the most unrealistic judgments, but only when they are answering recall questions, and even then the effects are weak.
people are not very good at regulating the realism of their memory confidence judgments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether people can improve the accuracy of their confidence judgments by deselecting the less accurate judgments.
the question of whether people have the ability to improve their accuracy in confidence judgments.
the accuracy of meta-memories and the ability to regulate the accuracy of these meta-memories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
people have some limited ability to regulate the accuracy of their confidence judgments.
confidence judgments can be regulated, but only to a limited extent, and that this regulation may be task dependent.
the participants in Experiment 1 did not regulate their confidence judgments to be more accurate and the participants in Experiment 2 regulated them only slightly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the accuracy of meta-memories is a function of both the quality of meta-memorial cues (in this case, the type of memory task) and the quality of meta-memory processes (in this case the ability to regulate the accuracy of meta-memory).
confidence judgments regulate both the realism and the accuracy of memory reports.
the accuracy of meta-memories is a function of how much the meta-memories are regulated by the metacognitive processes that underlie them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the realism of confidence judgments may be a useful cue for the regulation of report, but it is not the only cue.
people can improve the realism of some of their confidence judgments by deselecting the most unrealistic judgments.
the realism of confidence judgments is regulated by the type of task and the type of question, and that people have only limited ability to regulate the accuracy of confidence judgments.
